fields.name: issued_amount
fields.description: Principal loan amount originally issued (monetary amount)

fields.name: borrower_id
fields.description: Source-specific surrogate borrower identifier from bank2

conflicts.description: The customer primary-key attribute is named 'custid' in bank1 and 'customer_id' in bank2, referring to the same entity identity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into single attribute 'customer_id' in the target customer resource, with both source columns recorded as provenance.

conflicts.description: Customer name column uses the generic name 'name' in bank1 and 'customer_name' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'customer_name' to avoid ambiguity with other name columns.

conflicts.description: The customer telephone attribute is 'phone' in bank1 and 'mobileno' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'phone' as the canonical customer contact field.

conflicts.description: Branch name is 'name' in bank1 and 'branch_name' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'branch_name'.

conflicts.description: Branch address is 'address' in bank1 and 'branch_address' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'address' within the branch resource.

conflicts.description: Account primary key is 'account_no' in bank1 and 'account_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'account_id'.

conflicts.description: Account category attribute is abbreviated 'acc_type' in bank1 and 'account_type' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'account_type'.

conflicts.description: Account balance is 'balance' in bank1 and 'account_balance' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'balance' within the account resource.

conflicts.description: The loan principal is named generically 'amount' in bank1 and 'issued_amount' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'issued_amount' to disambiguate from other amount columns (transaction.amount, loan_payment.amount).

conflicts.description: bank1 contains inconsistent casing/homonyms for the same conceptual columns (e.g. 'branch_id' vs 'Branch_id', 'account_no' vs 'Account_No', 'loan_id' vs 'Loan_id', 'custid' vs 'Custid', 'bank_code' vs 'Bank_Code'). Several FK entries reference capitalized field names that do not exist as declared columns.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all identifiers to lower snake_case, collapsing each casing variant to a single canonical column and dropping the dangling capitalized FK references.

conflicts.description: bank1 models an explicit 'bank' entity while bank2 has no bank concept; branch-level attributes overlap the naming of bank-level attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Retained a distinct 'bank' resource (bank1 only) and kept 'branch' as the shared branch resource, avoiding name collision.

conflicts.description: Monetary values are typed as 'number' in bank1 (account.balance, loan.amount) but as 'integer' in bank2 (account_balance, issued_amount, remaining_amount, assets, transaction.amount, loan_payment.amount, card_limit).
conflicts.resolution: Unified all monetary columns to the generic 'number' type to accommodate fractional currency amounts without loss of precision.

conflicts.description: Identifier columns are consistently integer in both schemas; no numeric/string mismatch, but bank1.bank.code (string) vs branch-level code semantics differ.
conflicts.resolution: Kept all surrogate entity identifiers as integer; retained bank_code as string since it is a business code, not a numeric surrogate.

conflicts.description: bank1 represents the loan with a single 'amount', whereas bank2 decomposes the loan into 'issued_amount' and 'remaining_amount', implying distinct monetary semantics for issued vs outstanding amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped bank1.loan.amount to the issued principal ('issued_amount') and kept 'remaining_amount' as a separate bank2-only attribute, preserving both distinct semantics.

conflicts.description: Monetary balances/assets appear as integer counts in bank2 versus decimal 'number' in bank1, implying differing scale/precision conventions for the same financial quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a uniform fractional-capable representation ('number') for all monetary quantities and documented the semantic equivalence.

conflicts.description: The customer-account association is modeled as an explicit many-to-many relationship table (hold_by) in bank1 but as a single embedded 'account_id' FK on the customer row in bank2, conflating account ownership semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized both into the 'customer_account' bridge resource; the bank2 embedded FK is treated as one instance of the M:N ownership relation.

conflicts.description: 'phone' (generic) and 'mobileno' (mobile-specific) may denote the same contact channel but with differing specificity.
conflicts.resolution: Treated both as the same customer telephone attribute 'phone'.

conflicts.description: bank1 distinguishes bank-level name/address from branch-level name/address; bank2 only has branch-level data, risking conflation of bank vs branch identity.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved bank-level attributes only in the 'bank' resource and branch-level attributes in 'branch', keeping the two identity scopes semantically separated.

conflicts.description: bank1 heavily normalizes relationships into dedicated associative tables (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by), while bank2 embeds some relationships inline and introduces additional entities (borrower, loan_payment, transaction, customer_credit_card, banker_info) absent from bank1.
conflicts.resolution: Retained bank2-only entities as standalone resources and re-expressed bank1's associative tables as bridge resources; overlapping relations (availed_by/borrower) were merged.

conflicts.description: bank2 embeds the account relationship directly on the customer table (denormalized 1:1 style), conflicting with bank1's normalized associative structures.
conflicts.resolution: Removed the embedded FK from the unified customer entity and expressed the relation through the normalized customer_account bridge.

conflicts.description: bank1 decomposes the domain into a separate bank entity referenced by branch, whereas bank2 has no bank table — a difference in level of entity decomposition.
conflicts.resolution: Kept 'bank' as a distinct resource with branch.bank_code referencing it; bank2 branches simply leave bank_code null.

conflicts.description: bank1 stores branch-to-loan and branch-to-account links as separate many-to-many tables, while bank2 stores single branch FKs on loan and account.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved bank1's many-to-many bridge tables (branch_loan, branch_account) alongside the direct FK columns on loan/account.

conflicts.description: Customer-account relationship is many-to-many in bank1 (hold_by) but modeled as 1:1 in bank2 (single account_id on customer).
conflicts.resolution: Resolved to many-to-many via the customer_account bridge, treating bank2's single FK as a restricted instance.

conflicts.description: Customer-loan relationship is many-to-many in both schemas, but bank2's 'borrower' adds a surrogate primary key and reifies the relation as an entity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single many-to-many 'customer_loan' bridge keyed on (customer_id, loan_id), retaining the bank2 surrogate 'borrower_id' as a non-key attribute.

conflicts.description: Branch-loan is many-to-many (offer) in bank1 but many-to-one via a direct FK (loan.branch_id) in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the branch_loan bridge for the M:N relation while preserving the direct loan.branch_id FK.

conflicts.description: Branch-account is many-to-many (maintain) in bank1 but many-to-one via a direct FK (account.branch_id) in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the branch_account bridge while preserving the direct account.branch_id FK.

conflicts.description: bank2 introduces additional 1:1-style relationships (loan to account, credit card to account) not present in bank1, expanding relationship cardinalities across the unified model.
conflicts.resolution: Retained these as direct FK columns on their respective resources.

conflicts.description: Primary key of the customer entity is 'custid' in bank1 and 'customer_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key to 'customer_id' with both source keys listed in provenance.

conflicts.description: Primary key of the account entity is 'account_no' in bank1 and 'account_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key to 'account_id' with both source keys listed in provenance.

conflicts.description: Loan primary key is 'loan_id' in both schemas — consistent, but bank1 uses inconsistent casing in FK/PK declarations.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 'loan_id' as the unified primary key.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan relation uses a composite key in bank1 but a synthetic surrogate primary key 'borrower_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the composite key (customer_id, loan_id) for the unified customer_loan bridge, keeping borrower_id as a preserved surrogate attribute.

conflicts.description: bank1 identifies bank by a business code ('code') which is propagated as a foreign key on branch; bank2 has no equivalent key.
conflicts.resolution: Retained 'bank_code' as the bank primary key and as the branch foreign key.

conflicts.description: bank1 declares duplicate foreign keys using capitalized field names (Bank_Code, Branch_id, Loan_id, Account_No, Custid) that do not correspond to any declared columns — dangling/redundant key definitions.
conflicts.resolution: Consolidated each pair into a single canonical lowercase snake_case foreign key referencing the unified parent primary keys.

conflicts.description: Same customer identity attribute is named 'custid' in bank1 and 'customer_id' in bank2 (synonym divergence, and also the target PK of the merged customer entity).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to snake_case 'customer_id' as the target primary key of the customer resource.

conflicts.description: Customer name column is 'name' (bank1) vs 'customer_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name'.

conflicts.description: Customer telephone column named 'phone' (bank1) vs 'mobileno' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'phone'; both represent the customer contact number.

conflicts.description: Account identifier named 'account_no' (bank1) vs 'account_id' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_id' as the merged account primary key.

conflicts.description: Account type attribute named 'acc_type' (bank1) vs 'account_type' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_type'.

conflicts.description: Account balance column named 'balance' (bank1) vs 'account_balance' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'balance'.

conflicts.description: Branch name column named 'name' (bank1) vs 'branch_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name' inside the merged branch resource.

conflicts.description: Branch address column named 'address' (bank1) vs 'branch_address' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'address' inside the merged branch resource.

conflicts.description: The bank identifier 'code' is a bare homonym for the parent bank key.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to 'bank_code' to make the entity key explicit and consistent with the referencing column.

conflicts.description: Resource 'banker_info' and its 'banker_name' column diverge in naming style from the rest of the model.
conflicts.resolution: Resource renamed to 'banker' and 'banker_name' normalized to 'name'.

conflicts.description: bank1 uses verb-like association table names for its cross-entity links (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by).
conflicts.resolution: Retained meaningful association names offer/maintain for the branch links; renamed the merged person-loan and person-account links to the canonical 'customer_loan' and 'customer_account'.

conflicts.description: bank1 declares a second, PascalCase variant of each foreign key (Bank_Code, Branch_id, Custid, ...) that is a case-only homonym of the real column and points at non-existent PascalCase PKs.
conflicts.resolution: Treated as naming artifacts of the canonical lowercase columns and dropped; only one canonical FK per relationship is retained.

conflicts.description: Merged account balance is typed 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Widened to 'number' (the superset) so both sources load without precision loss.

conflicts.description: Loan monetary columns are 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized loan monetary columns to 'number' for cross-source homogeneity.

conflicts.description: Monetary columns declared as 'integer' in bank2 are inconsistent with the 'number' money representation chosen globally.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to 'number' so all monetary attributes share one representation; 'assets' stays integer as a count.

conflicts.description: bank1 models a loan's value as a single 'amount', whereas bank2 decomposes it into the issued principal and the outstanding balance — related but not identical concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as three distinct, semantically homogeneous attributes (amount, issued_amount, remaining_amount); 'amount' was NOT collapsed into 'issued_amount' because the exact same semantic attribute cannot be guaranteed.

conflicts.description: bank2 adds a 'branch.assets' quantitative attribute with no bank1 counterpart, and it is a monetary magnitude rather than an identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as its own integer attribute on the merged branch resource; no other source column was mapped to it.

conflicts.description: bank1 normalizes cross-entity relationships into dedicated associative tables (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by), while bank2 embeds the same relationships as foreign-key columns inside entity tables (account.branch_id, loan.branch_id, customer.account_id) or as a surrogate-keyed link table (borrower).
conflicts.resolution: Normalized consistently: many-to-many relationships are kept as bridge resources (offer, maintain, customer_loan, customer_account) that reference parent entities exclusively through foreign keys; single-valued entity ownership links that both sources agree on (account.branch_id, loan.branch_id) are kept as entity foreign keys.

conflicts.description: bank2 denormalizes the customer-to-account link directly onto the customer entity, whereas bank1 keeps it in a separate relationship table.
conflicts.resolution: Folded into the customer_account bridge to avoid duplicating the relationship in two places.

conflicts.description: Customer-account relationship is many-to-many in bank1 (hold_by composite key) but many-to-one in bank2 (customer.account_id single FK).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to the more general N:M bridge 'customer_account' (composite PK customer_id, account_id), which subsumes bank2's N:1 usage.

conflicts.description: Both sources model customer-loan as a many-to-many association but with different structures (composite-key table vs surrogate-keyed entity).
conflicts.resolution: Merged into a single N:M bridge 'customer_loan' with composite PK (customer_id, loan_id).

conflicts.description: Branch-loan relationship appears as an N:M association (offer) in bank1 and as an N:1 ownership FK (loan.branch_id) in bank2; likewise bank1.maintain vs account.branch_id for branch-account.
conflicts.resolution: Both facets are semantically distinct (branch that offers/maintains vs branch that owns) and are each present in both sources, so the association (offer/maintain) and the ownership FK (branch_id) are retained as separate structures rather than collapsed.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan association uses a composite natural key in bank1 (custid, loan_id) but a synthetic surrogate key in bank2 (borrower_id).
conflicts.resolution: Unified on the composite natural key (customer_id, loan_id) for the merged customer_loan bridge; the bank2 surrogate borrower_id carries no source-independent counterpart and is dropped.

conflicts.description: bank1's foreign key declarations reference PascalCase key columns that do not exist as fields in the referenced resources, duplicating the valid lowercase FK declarations.
conflicts.resolution: Deduplicated to a single canonical FK per relationship, pointing at the merged snake_case primary keys.

conflicts.description: bank2 declares every foreign key twice (identical duplicate entries), indicating redundant key metadata.
conflicts.resolution: Deduplicated to one foreign-key declaration per relationship in the target schema.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification differs by naming and representation between sources for the two shared core entities.
conflicts.resolution: Each shared entity key unified to a single canonical PK (customer_id, account_id) whose provenance lists both source primary keys.

conflicts.description: Customer primary key is named 'custid' in bank1 but 'customer_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'customer_id' following the bank2 snake_case convention; both identifiers are grouped in the same column provenance.

conflicts.description: Customer name attribute named 'name' (bank1) vs 'customer_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name' as the atomic attribute name for the customer resource.

conflicts.description: Contact number stored as 'phone' (bank1) vs 'mobileno' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'phone' as the canonical mobile/telephone attribute.

conflicts.description: Branch label named 'name' (bank1) vs 'branch_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name' within the branch resource.

conflicts.description: Branch address named 'address' (bank1) vs 'branch_address' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'address' within the branch resource.

conflicts.description: Account type attribute abbreviated as 'acc_type' (bank1) vs 'account_type' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_type' using the fully spelled snake_case name.

conflicts.description: Account balance named 'balance' (bank1) vs 'account_balance' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'balance' within the account resource.

conflicts.description: Account identifier named 'account_no' (bank1) vs 'account_id' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_id' as the account primary key column name.

conflicts.description: Resource 'banker_info' and column 'banker_name' carry redundant entity prefixes relative to the target naming scheme.
conflicts.resolution: Resource renamed to 'banker' and column to 'name' for a normalized, consistent naming convention.

conflicts.description: Relationship resources use heterogeneous, verb-based names (hold_by, availed_by, maintain, offer) in bank1 while bank2 names the analogous bridge 'borrower' as if it were an entity.
conflicts.resolution: Bridge resources renamed to a consistent composite <entity>_<entity> convention (customer_account, customer_loan, branch_account, branch_loan).

conflicts.description: Resource named 'customer_credit_card' embeds the parent entity name prefix.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to 'credit_card'; the customer linkage is captured through the customer_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: Account balance is declared 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted to 'number' to preserve fractional monetary precision without loss across both sources.

conflicts.description: Loan principal is 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted to 'number' so the unified 'issued_amount' column accommodates both representations.

conflicts.description: All bank2 monetary/quantitative attributes (transaction amount, loan payment amount, card limit, branch assets) are declared 'integer', whereas bank1 monetary attributes use 'number'.
conflicts.resolution: Monetary measures normalized to 'number'; 'assets' retained as 'integer' since it is a count-like magnitude only present in bank2.

conflicts.description: Both columns denote the loan principal, but bank1 labels it generically as 'amount' while bank2 distinguishes 'issued_amount' from 'remaining_amount'.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into 'issued_amount' as the single principal-amount attribute; the assumption that bank1 'amount' equals the issued principal is documented, and 'remaining_amount' is kept as a distinct attribute.

conflicts.description: Monetary scale representation differs: bank2 models money as whole-number integers while bank1 permits decimal numbers, implying different implicit precision/scale (e.g., whole currency units vs. fractional).
conflicts.resolution: All monetary quantities unified to the 'number' type so a single decimal currency unit convention applies across the global schema.

conflicts.description: Categorical account-type values may follow different domain encodings between the two sources.
conflicts.resolution: Both mapped to a single 'account_type' string attribute; value-level harmonization is deferred to the transformation layer.

conflicts.description: The customer-account linkage is modeled as an explicit many-to-many bridge (hold_by) in bank1, but embedded as a single FK attribute (account_id) on the customer table in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into a dedicated bridge resource 'customer_account' with composite key (customer_id, account_id), preserving both the bank1 bridge rows and the bank2 embedded linkage.

conflicts.description: The same customer-loan relationship is represented by two separate bridge structures with different naming and key strategies.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into one bridge resource 'customer_loan' (customer_id, loan_id), merging provenance from availed_by and borrower.

conflicts.description: Branch-loan association exists simultaneously as an explicit bridge (offer) and as a direct FK (loan.branch_id) in bank1, while bank2 only uses the direct FK.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations retained: 'branch_loan' bridge preserves the M:N association and 'loan.branch_id' preserves the direct FK.

conflicts.description: Branch-account association exists as both an explicit bridge (maintain) and a direct FK in bank1, while bank2 relies only on the direct FK.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations retained: 'branch_account' bridge preserves the M:N association and 'account.branch_id' preserves the direct FK.

conflicts.description: bank1 decomposes an explicit 'bank' parent entity referenced by branch.bank_code, whereas bank2 has no bank entity and instead stores branch-level 'assets'.
conflicts.resolution: The 'bank' entity is retained as a top-level resource and branch.bank_code is preserved as an optional FK; the bank2-only 'assets' attribute is added to the unified branch resource.

conflicts.description: bank2 embeds account linkage directly inside customer and loan, mixing associative relationships into entity tables.
conflicts.resolution: Account relationships re-expressed through normalized FK/bridge columns so entity tables hold only atomic attributes.

conflicts.description: Customer-account relationship is many-to-many in bank1 (via hold_by) but one-to-many/one-to-one in bank2 (account_id on customer).
conflicts.resolution: Resolved to a many-to-many bridge 'customer_account' to safely accommodate both cardinalities.

conflicts.description: bank1 expresses the branch-loan relationship as both M:N (offer) and N:1 (loan.branch_id), which is redundant; bank2 expresses it only as N:1.
conflicts.resolution: N:1 enforced via loan.branch_id; the residual M:N is retained explicitly as 'branch_loan' so no source association is discarded.

conflicts.description: Both sources model the customer-loan linkage as M:N, but bank2 decorates the bridge with an extra surrogate identity while bank1 uses the natural pair.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to a single M:N bridge 'customer_loan' keyed on the natural pair (customer_id, loan_id).

conflicts.description: bank1 identifies the bank entity with a string natural key 'code', while branches (and all other entities) use integer surrogate keys.
conflicts.resolution: Bank key retained as the string primary key 'bank_code'; it is referenced by an optional FK from branch without altering the integer surrogate keys used elsewhere.

conflicts.description: bank1 bridge tables are keyed by natural composite keys, whereas bank2.borrower introduces a surrogate 'borrower_id' primary key in addition to its natural (customer_id, loan_id) pair.
conflicts.resolution: All bridges unified on natural composite primary keys; the bank2 surrogate borrower_id is dropped as redundant, with the natural key columns carrying provenance.

conflicts.description: bank1 declares the same foreign key twice using inconsistent casing (e.g., bank_code/Bank_Code, branch_id/Branch_id), implying duplicate or phantom key references.
conflicts.resolution: De-duplicated into single, consistently snake_case foreign keys; the casing variants are consolidated into the lowercase column provenance.

conflicts.description: bank2 restates identical foreign key declarations twice per relationship (exact duplicates).
conflicts.resolution: Collapsed to a single foreign key definition per relationship in the unified schema.

conflicts.description: bank2 defines account_id as a mandatory foreign key on customer, creating a key dependency in the opposite direction of bank1's customer->account bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Customer-to-account dependency re-expressed as the 'customer_account' bridge, removing the embedded FK from the customer entity.
